gaps.quote: By the telescoping, the route applies $\varepsilon_w D_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$
gaps.note: The telescoping identity only multiplies the frame changes along the edges of one route; the gates on that route also combine the value with other wires' values. The page never connects the frames to the scalar network's signed permutation (that at every address the logical output at role rho(w) is epsilon_w times the logical input at w, so the stored output is epsilon_w D_sink times D_source inverse of the stored input), so the reader cannot see why the whole network's map from input w to output rho(w) is this operator rather than something involving the gates.

gaps.term: every role keeps the endpoint operator
gaps.quote: Every role keeps the endpoint operator (cited), auxiliary roles included.
gaps.note: The page does not say what it means for a role to 'keep' its endpoint operator or what role this cited claim plays. For a scratch role it would mean the value returns multiplied by D_sink(w) D_source(w)^{-1}, which is not the identity unless the two frames agree, yet the page opened by saying the network restores every auxiliary value; the reader cannot reconcile the two or tell how scratch values are actually restored.
